Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

only adverb

no more than; just

also just, merely, simply, not only … but also, mere, a mere, the mere, only if

classical

Hor. S. 1.9.3: nōtus mihi nōmine tantum (Lewis & Short)
Mart. 1.32.2: hoc tantum possum dīcere

tantum

adverb · Wiktionary

only, merely, just

After the word it limits. Strengthened, tantummodo: velīs tantummodo, you have only to want it (Hor. S. 1.9.54, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • modo — only; with a command, just …!

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 674: Sequere hāc mē modo; Cic. Fam. 16.11.1: modo fac, nē quid aliud cūrēs (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    The “just” of requests: Properā modo, just hurry (Plaut. Men. 215). With numbers: semel modo, only once (Plaut. Poen. 1.3.30, Lewis & Short).

  • sōlum — only, alone

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.22: nōn nōbīs sōlum nātī sumus; Caes. BG 1.12 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 354 · Wiktionary

    Mostly in nōn sōlum … sed etiam, not only … but also; on its own it is rarer (Lewis & Short). Sōlummodo is late.

  • dumtaxat — only, merely; at least as far as … goes

    adverb, after the word it limits · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.3 fin.: nōs animō dumtaxat vigēmus (Lewis & Short); Cic. N. D. 2.47: sint ista pulchriōra dumtaxat aspectū (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: “to this extent, so far”: it limits what goes before, animō dumtaxat, in spirit only. A word of prose, rarer than tantum and modo.

Examples

  • nōn amō tē, Sabidī, nec possum dīcere quārē: hoc tantum possum dīcere, nōn amō tē

    I don’t like you, Sabidius, and I can’t say why: all I can say is this, I don’t like youMart. 1.32.1–2

  • Sequere hāc mē modo … nē timē.

    Just follow me this way … don’t be afraid.Plaut. Amph. 674

  • nōn nōbīs sōlum nātī sumus

    we are not born for ourselves aloneCic. Off. 1.22

  • tantummodo sī

    only ifTraupman 69

See also only, just, wish, once.
